design: Tier 1, no migration (spec_document_merges exists since 0074). The fold is spec_service.merge_document with a payload the Hub builds, so validation, identity minting, rendering and the audit row are the merge's own. Key rule: <change-slug>-<key>, the slug trimmed from the right so the whole key is at most 64 characters (KEY_RE, spec_payload.py:42); the dialog lets the operator rename. The archive guard lives in spec_lifecycle.transition beside the operator check, so every archive path meets it; no_capability_change rides PhaseRequest. HAZARDS: the UI bundle reaches :8000's app at its next reload, and from :8000's next restart a direct capability content write is refused there too (the operator's app never makes one; only scripts did). Rollback: revert the commits; no data changes shape.

problem: Closing a change has needed a hand-written script per change. The merge route (spec.py:2260) exists but takes the capability's whole new payload and has no app screen (the-corpus-keeps-what-shipped design D7), so every reconcile so far went through PUT .../content instead (scripts/drive/reconcile_f4xx.py, reconcile_f509.py, reconcile_f531.py): spec_document_merges holds 0 rows on :8010. Archive checks only that the actor is the operator (spec_lifecycle.py:319), so nothing stopped a shipped change being archived unfolded, and nothing noticed F509's three slices sat in no capability for two days (DEAD-ENDS 2026-10-08).

requirements.rationale: The operator reviews text instead of writing it; most reconciles so far copied the change's statements unchanged.
requirements.statement: For an approved change-spec and a named capability document, the Hub MUST return a fold draft: the capability's current payload with each of the change's requirements appended verbatim under the key <change-slug>-<key> (the change's folder name, trimmed so the key is at most 64 characters), each acceptance criterion of those requirements appended with its requirement re-pointed at the new key, and every draft key that already exists in the capability reported as a collision rather than overwritten.

requirements.rationale: Replaces the per-change reconcile scripts with one audited operator action; a change touching two capabilities is folded twice, archiving on the second.
requirements.statement: The operator MUST be able to fold an approved change-spec into a capability document in one request, choosing which of the change's requirements to fold (default all), each optionally with an edited key, statement or modal, or naming an existing capability requirement it replaces; the fold MUST write through the merge (one spec_document_merges row naming the change and one merged event) and, unless told not to, move the change to archived in the same transaction. It MUST be refused before anything is written when the change is not approved, a task of it is still open, a named requirement is not the change's, a key collides without naming what it replaces, a replaced key is not the capability's, or the target is not a capability document.

requirements.rationale: archived has no way back; a shipped change whose requirements live nowhere else must not become history (F509).
requirements.statement: Archiving an approved change-spec MUST be refused, naming what is missing, unless every task the document declared is approved or rejected and either a merge names the change or the operator states no_capability_change with a non-empty reason. Other kinds and the existing exploring/proposed archive rule are unchanged.

requirements.rationale: Every capability change then has an audit row saying which change it came from, or that it was an edit; the original design said capability documents are written only by merge.
requirements.statement: A capability document's content MUST change only through a merge: a direct content write to a capability document is refused with a code naming the merge route, and a merge naming no change is accepted as an operator edit and recorded as one. Creating a capability document is unchanged.

requirements.rationale: The close-out becomes something the operator does in the app, and an unfolded shipped change is visible where the operator already looks.
requirements.statement: The document view of an approved change-spec MUST carry fold_state (tasks_open, ready, or folded with the capability paths it was folded into), and the app's phase bar MUST show a ready change as shipped but not yet in a capability, with a Fold into capability action (capability picker, the draft's requirements with editable key and statement, an archive option on by default, confirm) and an Archive without a capability change action that asks for a reason.

summary: The operator closes a finished change from the app: the Hub drafts the capability's new content by copying the change's requirements and criteria in, the operator may edit the draft, and one confirm merges it (audited) and archives the change. Archiving a change is refused until its tasks are done and it was folded somewhere, or the operator says it changes no capability. A capability's content changes only through a merge.
